archimate:Folder.name: 2 Business Process Architecture
archimate:Folder.documentation:
Within the Business Architecture of the Statistical Architecture Framework (SAF), business processes describe the dynamic dimension of how a statistical organization operates — how business functions are organized into coherent sequences of activities to achieve defined outcomes, deliver services, and produce statistical or analytical outputs. Business processes are the operational realization of the organization’s value streams, linking the strategic “why” and the structural “what” of the organization to the executable “how” of daily operations.
In the context of the SAF, business processes provide a standardized and comparable representation of how statistical activities are carried out across organizations. They describe the flow of work that transforms data inputs into valuable outputs such as indicators, analyses, and publications, while ensuring adherence to principles of quality, transparency, and governance. Each process is designed to support one or more SAF business capabilities and is aligned with internationally recognized models such as the Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GSBPM).
Business processes are supported by a variety of specific business functions. These functions represent the stable, reusable building blocks of business behavior — encapsulating what the organization does, independent of when or how often it is done. For example, functions such as Data Validation, Quality Assessment, or Metadata Management can be invoked by multiple processes, regardless of their position within the process flow. This separation ensures flexibility, reusability, and standardization across the statistical value chain, enabling the organization to evolve or reconfigure its operational workflows without redefining its core business logic.
While business processes represent the orchestration of activities, business functions capture the capabilities or competencies that underpin those activities. This distinction is critical within the SAF: functions exist independently of the specific process sequence in which they are used, allowing for modularity and interoperability. This modular design supports the modernization goals of the SAF by enabling statistical organizations to automate, combine, or re-engineer business processes without losing conceptual consistency or alignment with their enterprise architecture.
Business services act as the interface between the organization’s internal processes and its users — whether internal analysts, external researchers, partner institutions, or the public. They expose the underlying processes and functions as accessible, governed, and well-defined service offerings that fulfill specific business needs. A business service may, for example, represent a data access service, metadata query service, or quality reporting service, each backed by one or more business processes. In this way, business services make the outcomes of internal operations visible, consumable, and measurable, enabling a service-oriented and data-centric statistical organization.
The outcomes of business processes and services are captured as business artefacts — the tangible or intangible outputs produced by the organization’s activities. Artefacts represent the information or deliverables that carry business value, such as statistical datasets, analytical reports, quality statements, or methodological documentation. Within the SAF, these artefacts are treated as essential traceable entities, forming part of the organization’s broader information architecture and contributing to transparency, accountability, and reusability of results.
Together, business processes, functions, services, and artefacts form a cohesive system that describes how the statistical enterprise operates. Business processes ensure that organizational goals are achieved through well-defined and controlled sequences of actions; business functions define the reusable abilities that perform those actions; business services expose those capabilities to users; and business artefacts represent the measurable outcomes of business value creation.
By structuring these components according to the ArchiMate modeling language and TOGAF’s enterprise architecture principles, the SAF enables statistical organizations to describe, analyze, and improve their operational models in a standardized, interoperable way. This ensures that modernization efforts—such as automation, data integration, or the introduction of AI-assisted processes—are grounded in a clear understanding of how the business truly operates and where value is created across the statistical system.
In essence, the Business Processes layer of the Statistical Architecture Framework provides the operational backbone of the statistical organization. It connects strategy to execution, capability to performance, and input to output. It allows statistical organizations to maintain coherence in a rapidly evolving digital and data-driven environment—ensuring that every transformation, from data collection to dissemination, remains aligned with business purpose, regulatory compliance, and the shared mission of producing trustworthy and high-quality statistics for society.
